messages: The AI rules located emphasise human responsibility and transparency but differ on accepted uses and disclosure exemptions. A purposive sample and A/NL records do not establish universal consensus.
Reviewing is not a single task

LMS, Copernicus, RBG and ESA allow language assistance under conditions; this does not authorise delegating scientific assessment. JAMA and JSWE have specific prohibitions. Confidentiality, tools and disclosure must be checked separately.

Methods, Acknowledgements, cover letters, dedicated sections and references may be cumulative requirements or conditional alternatives. Thieme, LMS and Scientia Agricola request declarations even of non-use; this requirement should not be extended to other titles without evidence.
Images: a concept is not data

IOP and Taylor & Francis allow conceptual illustrations; Elsevier distinguishes explanatory images, data-derived visualisations and experimental images. Do not confuse illustration permission with authorisation to fabricate evidence.
Brazil: dataset description, not a census

29 of the dataset’s 36 Brazilian journals have an AI clause. RAE and Educação & Sociedade prohibit generating text, subject to the exceptions described in the notes. RBCS-ANPOCS’s current policy allows assistance with disclosure and human responsibility, while restricting images. Absence of a clause in a corpus does not establish absence throughout an institution.
On 7 November 2026, all 165 records were reconciled across the four policy fields. The review added 16 policies and updated 5 existing records.
cross: Purposive inventory of 165 identities. On 7 November 2026, all 165 records were reconciled across the four policy fields. The review added 16 policies and updated 5 existing records. Proportions describe the inventory.
112 Allowed, 22 Restricted, 11 Prohibited, 17 No rule located and 3 Not applicable. Codes summarise writing policy. The notes describe exceptions and AI as a research method.
99 records make use conditional, 13 prohibit it and 53 have no coded provision. The notes describe the scope and conditions.
Representative illustrations, computational visualisations and experimental images are not interchangeable categories. Read the entity's note and source before producing or altering a figure.
Multiple locations includes cumulative requirements and alternatives depending on the use or article structure. It does not mean all sections are always mandatory.
32/39 journals have a coded rule (82% of the sample). 15/39 have a coded reviewer provision. The denominators describe the sample.

brasil: **Brazilian sample.** 32 of 39 journals have a coded rule (82%). Among them, 21 allow, 8 restrict and 3 prohibit text generation.

**New entries.** Revista da Abralin, Cadernos de Linguística and Trabalhos em Linguística Aplicada each have their own rules. Edusp is included as a book publisher and is excluded from the journal denominator.

**Reviewers:** RBG allows improving the language of a human review within limits; Gestão & Produção and RBLA allow auxiliary assistance with safeguards. RAE prohibits reviewing use. Conditional does not mean automatic assessment is allowed.

**Disclosure:** Scientia Agricola requires Methods for AI use plus a statement before References; the manuscript-format section requires that statement even when AI was not used. The previous description was corrected. In Educação & Sociedade, auxiliary use is mentioned at the end without a mandatory section heading.

**SciELO:** the preliminary guide of 14 September 2023 advises transparency in the Abstract and Methods or equivalent. Adoption and exceptions must be confirmed in journal instructions; the guide does not establish an identical rule throughout the network.

**CNPq and other agencies:** CNPq's official March 2026 rule was read: assistive use requires responsibility and transparency; confidential third-party proposals must not be submitted to external tools. This is not a prohibition of every form of reviewer assistance. The FAPESP/CAPES/FAPEG aggregate remains separate and does not inherit CNPq's rule.
**Coverage.** 39/39 Brazilian journals reconciled on 7 November. A/NL describe the corpus and searches recorded in the history.
checks: **Target and role:** read the journal/event rules for the article type and your role. The publisher's general policy alone does not establish every title's operational rule.

**Confidentiality:** do not enter third-party manuscripts or proposals into services without authorisation and protection consistent with the applicable policy. A paid account does not guarantee privacy by itself.
**Record:** retain tool, version, date, task, relevant prompts and human verification. Confirm authorship, references, numbers and results in original sources.
**Disclosure:** check cumulative or alternative locations, format and exemptions. Do not assume language editing always requires disclosure or is always exempt.
**Method:** report AI use in collection, processing, analysis or visualisation reproducibly; this is not equivalent to permission to generate scientific text.
**Images:** distinguish conceptual illustrations, data-derived graphs and experimental images. Never fabricate evidence. Observe permission, captions and general declarations when required.
**Review:** judgement and responsibility remain human. Permitted language assistance does not authorise uploading the manuscript, automated summarisation or generating an assessment.
**Proposals:** check the agency and call. NSF encourages transparency in the project description; UKRI exempts minimal use and limits assessors to language without confidential content.
**Edition limitation:** check the review history. An access or normative-confirmation gap is neither permission nor absence or revocation of a rule.

metodo: Question

How scientific societies, publishers, journals, ethics bodies and funding agencies regulate generative-AI use in research, manuscript writing and peer review, and how this varies across CNPq's broad research areas.
Historical baseline

Purposive survey compiled on 14–16 October 2026, with an initial reference date of 16 October. The latest full review, after compilation, is dated 7 November 2026 and documented in the history. Maintenance does not retroactively certify the compilation’s reading or methodological independence. This is neither a PRISMA review nor a worldwide census.
Review of 7 November 2026

On 7 November 2026, all 165 records were reconciled across the four policy fields. The review added 16 policies and updated 5 existing records. The history preserves sources, actual consultation times, discovery results and decisions by entity.
Sample

149 identities preserved and 16 added after Portuguese and English searches for societies, publishers and journals. The final inventory has 165 identities and 39 Brazilian journals. Deduplication uses identity and scope.
Coding

Four fields: author text generation/editing, disclosure, reviewing/editing, and images/data. Multiple locations may indicate cumulative requirements or alternatives depending on use/article structure. No rule located and Not addressed express limits of the examined scope, never implicit permission.
Verification

P = primary source; S = secondary source; H = inherited rule with applicable adoption demonstrated; A = no specific clause in the stated corpus; NL = not located in the bounded search. Consult individual outcomes in the history. A/NL prove neither institutional absence nor permission to use AI. Publisher affiliation alone does not establish a specific instruction.
Evidence and dates

The history records owner, section, actual consultation time, normative-text hash and field-level decisions. Comparison uses the full 24 October review and the partial 31 October update. Consultation dates and policy dates are independent.
Limits
165 of 165 records reconciled. Candidates lacking evidence remain in the discovery history. The sample is purposive and coding was AI-assisted.
Policy and practice

Studies in the evidence section use different corpora, dates and methods; estimates of linguistic traces do not identify individual use with certainty and are not directly comparable to disclosure rates. They do not causally establish a policy's effectiveness. Historical estimates were not reanalysed in this maintenance.
AI-use disclosure

Initial compilation with Claude (Anthropic). Reviews with Codex (OpenAI) for source comparison, coding, editorial translation, exports and testing. Editorial responsibility rests with the Observatory. No independent duplicate extraction.
Dataset and traceability

JSON, CSV and XLSX derive from the same dataset. The historical v4 to v5 column and the codebook are preserved. The dated history records sources, decisions, prospecting and outstanding work. All four exports preserve identities, codes, years and URLs. The English translation is editorial and unofficial.
